newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures finish sharply higher post-jobs.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures finish sharply higher post-jobs.

text.p: U.S. debt futures finished sharply higher after a session of heavy trading, fueled by the unexpected 40,000 drop in September U.S. jobs.
"You can't deny it looks good," a futures analyst said.

December Treasury bond futures closed well above its 200-day moving average for the first time in months and close to its session high, providing more bullish fodder for early next week, some traders said.
In the short end, trading was brisk all day, with good two-way flows seen much of the afternoon. Resistance in March Euros for Monday was seen from 94.37 to 94.40, traders said.

U.S. jobs fell 40,000 in September, a sharp contrast from the 166,000 increase that was forecast and the downwardly revised 241,000 gain in August. The jobless rate was reported at 5.2 percent from 5.1 in August.

After the release of the data, December T-bonds surged to a 6-1/2 month high and matched the session high from March 25 before scaling back slightly as traders focused on the 0.5-percent rise in hourly wages. Some worried that wages were in a solid uptrend.
But the market soon shook off the wage-worries and trekked back to the top of the day's range.
One trader called the rally orderly and said the tone should be firm heading into next week's inflation data.
While some called for continued gains early next week, others said the market was due to retreat after this steep move.

"The tendency is for a market once it penetrates (the 200-day moving) average to come and test it on the other side, so this will be support," said Jim Hyerczyk, president of JAH Research and Trading. "110-26/32 is going to be real critical," he said. December T-bonds rallied above and close well-above the 200-day moving average at 110-28/32 on Friday.
"It's a pretty tough average to hold above," Hyerczyk said.
Traders pegged the 111-28/32 double top and 112-00 resistance for Monday in December T-bonds.

December Treasury bond futures finished up 1-12/32 at 111-22/32, muni-bonds were 1-1/32 higher at 116-9/32, and March Euros rose 15 basis points at 94.33. March T-bills were up 15 basis points at 94.85.
